structures.name: Habenula
structures.about: The habenula is located posterior and dorsal to the main body of the thalamus. It is involved in a wide array of functions, including pain processing, stress response, and reward evaluation.

structures.name: Thalamus
structures.about: The thalamus is a grey matter structure located in the diencephalon. It acts as a sensory and motor relay.

structures.name: Corpus Callosum
structures.about: The corpus callosum is a structure made up of dense white matter fibers that connect the two hemispheres of the brain.

structures.name: Arbor Vitae
structures.about: The arbor vitae is the white matter of the cerebellum. It has a tree-like appearance from a midsagittal view.

structures.name: Cerebral Aqueduct
structures.about: The cerebral aqueduct is a narrow canal that runs through the midbrain (mesencephalon), connecting the third and forth ventricles.

structures.name: Third Ventricle
structures.about: The third ventricle is a more narrow cavity spanning the midline in the area around the thalamus

structures.name: Cingulate Gyrus
structures.about: The cingulate gyrus is grey matter just dorsal to the corpus callosum. It is a part of the limbic system and acts as an integrative hub of emotions, sensation, and behavioral regulation.

structures.name: Hypothalamus
structures.about: The hypothalamus is ventral to the thalamus and is involved in homeostatic regulation, including temperature balance, fluid balance, and energy balance.

structures.name: Optic Chiasm
structures.about: The optic chiasm is the point at which some of the fibers traveling down the optic nerve cross to the contralateral side of the body on their way to the lateral geniculate nucleus of the thalamus.

structures.name: Pineal Body
structures.about: The pineal body is involved in the regulation of waking/sleeping cycles, and releases the hormone melatonin.

structures.name: Superior Colliculus
structures.about: The superior colliculus is a structure in the tectum of the midbrain. This area is important for visual reflexes, gaze shifting, and eye movements.

structures.name: Inferior Colliculus
structures.about: The inferior colliculus is a structure in the tectum of the midbrain. It relays auditory information to the auditory cortex, and is also involved in generating startle responses as well as basic discrimination of pitch and rhythm.

structures.name: Fornix
structures.about: The fornix is the primary output tract from the hippocampus.

structures.name: Septum Pellucidum
structures.about: The septum pellucidum is a thin membrane located at the midline. It separates the lateral ventricles from each other.

structures.name: Posterior Commissure
structures.about: The posterior commissure is a bundle of fibers connecting the hemispheres, and is found just ventral to the pineal body and habenula.

structures.name: Anterior Commissure
structures.about: The anterior commissure is a small bundle of fibers that crosses the midline, connecting the amygdalae, olfactory areas, and parts of the temporal lobe across hemispheres. From a midsagittal view, it appears as a small while dot below the anterior portion of the fornix and anterior to the thalamus.

structures.name: Central Sulcus
structures.about: The central sulcus is a major sulcus separating the frontal lobe from the parietal lobe.

structures.name: Precentral Gyrus
structures.about: The precentral gyrus is the location of the primary motor cortex.

structures.name: Postcentral Gyrus
structures.about: The postcentral gyrus is the location of the primary somatosensory cortex.

structures.name: Mammillary Bodies
structures.about: The mammillary bodies are paired nuclei in the hypothalamus involved in memory circuits.

structures.name: Pons
structures.about: The pons is a brainstem structure that relays signals between the cerebrum and cerebellum.

structures.name: Fourth Ventricle
structures.about: The fourth ventricle is a CSF-filled cavity between the pons, medulla, and cerebellum.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.about: The cerebellum is a hindbrain structure that coordinates voluntary movement, balance, and motor learning.

structures.name: Tegmentum
structures.about: The tegmentum is the ventral portion of the midbrain, containing nuclei and fiber tracts involved in motor control and arousal.

structures.name: Medulla
structures.about: The medulla oblongata is the caudal-most region of the brainstem, regulating autonomic functions such as breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure.
